name: PT Astra International Tbk

frontmatter.title: Astra International: a cash-generative conglomerate at the market's own discount
frontmatter.summary: Update after Q3-2026. The nine-month actuals were already in the published update; the 28 October and 29 October stories re-report that release. This revision widens the financing block's equity base to match its income, deducts parent-entity net debt instead of adding group net cash, and carries the buyback at the prior programme's pace. ADD at Rp4,849.
thesis: The look-through sum-of-the-parts marks the parts at Rp4,514 after a 25% discount, essentially the 24.6% discount the price implies, so the expected return is the cost-of-equity roll plus the dividend rather than an assumed convergence of the discount [S2, S14].

The operating blocks still earn above the cost of equity: the financing arm is carried at a premium to book even after widening its equity base to include its joint-venture investments of IDR9.28tn, the base that matches an income line carrying their results [S15].

The clean nine-month result was flat on the prior year despite the Martabe outage and the coal-quota hit, with automotive and financial services growing and mining profit back to year-on-year growth in the third quarter [S14].
The bear case is a discount widening to the top of its persistent range with mining weak and credit costs higher; it is carried explicitly at Rp3,917 [S14, S5].

catalysts.event: Astra voluntary tender offer for Astra Otoparts closes
FY2026 audited results, final dividend and buyback-execution disclosure

frontmatter.catalyst_note: The Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised and on-going but has no disclosed end date or pace [S8, S14, S16], so it is not a dated narrowing catalyst and the base does not rely on it. 30 April 2027 is the FY2026 audited-results date on the prior-year cadence [S4], when buyback execution must be disclosed; it dates the disclosure, not the action. The base is a cost-of-equity return call and the narrowing sits in the bull case.

blocks.text: **The news adds nothing.** The 28 October net-profit story and the 29 October revenue story are re-reports of the same 28 October release our published update already carried: every figure they cite, including flat revenue of IDR243.87tn, is in the release and the LK, they add no operating fact, and change neither the forecast nor the mark [S17, S12, S14, S15].

**What changed in this revision.** The nine-month reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, but IDR2.96tn of the gap is a non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge; clean of it, profit was IDR24.57tn on revenue of IDR243.87tn [S14, S15]. Mining returned to year-on-year growth in the third quarter after a first half distorted by the Martabe outage and the coal quota [S14]. We stay at **ADD** with a target of Rp4,849 against Rp4,540, an expected total return of 16.1% including Rp420 of dividends [S14, S15]. Two construction corrections cut the mark: the financing block's equity base now includes its joint-venture investments of IDR9.28tn to match the income basis [S15], and the bridge deducts parent-entity net debt rather than group net cash already inside the marks [S15, S14]. With both, the sum-of-the-parts is Rp4,514, essentially at the price, and the ADD is the 14.9% cost-of-equity roll net of the dividend — a return call, not a discount-narrowing call [S15, S0].

The market is valuing the group as one declining business while its largest halves grow: automotive net income rose to IDR9.79tn and financial services to IDR7.15tn over nine months, while mining fell to IDR5.07tn [S14], and those three earn about nine tenths of group profit [S2, S3]. The mining downturn is real but bounded [S14].

Astra International is one of Indonesia's largest listed companies: more than three hundred subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates spanning vehicles, heavy equipment, mining, plantations, toll roads, IT and property [S2]. From the first half of 2026 it reports Automotive, Financial Services and Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment as its three Core Businesses, with everything else in Others [S2, S3].

On the audited FY2025 divisional basis, net income attributable to the parent split as follows: Automotive & Mobility IDR11.37tn, Financial Services IDR8.95tn, Heavy Equipment, Mining, Construction & Energy IDR9.10tn, Agribusiness IDR1.17tn, Infrastructure IDR1.26tn, Information Technology IDR0.21tn and Property IDR0.72tn [S4]. Automotive is distribution and retail finance on Toyota, Daihatsu, the Honda motorcycle joint venture and Otoparts; Mining Solutions & Heavy Equipment is United Tractors, the largest earnings-volatility source [S4].

Strategy changed materially in 2026: a May roadmap focused the group on three core businesses, put every wider business under an earn-or-reallocate test, and tied leadership incentives to total shareholder return [S11]; in July shareholders approved a new buyback and a management share plan [S8]. Control sits with Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd at 50.1% of the shares, part of the Jardine Matheson group, with a 49.0% free float [S6, S0].

Astra began as a trading company and grew into a conglomerate by partnering with Japanese industrial groups across
vehicles, components and heavy machinery, then adding financial services. Much of its profit still comes from joint
ventures where it holds a minority economic interest but a controlling operating role.

The Indonesian car market is the swing factor. National car sales fell through 2025, when the company said its share could reach 51.0% [S4]. They turned hard in 2026: national wholesales reached 679,000 units in the first nine months, up about a fifth, while Astra's own car sales grew more slowly and its share normalised to 49.0% [S14, S7]. The industry body expects the 850,000-unit full-year target to be met [S7]. The recovery is incomplete: middle-income buyers have not returned and financing access remains the constraint [S9]. Motorcycles are the steadier franchise, with Honda holding 77.0% of the market [S14].

The heavy-equipment and mining complex is the mirror image, and the third quarter marked a turn. Over nine months Komatsu unit sales fell to 3,000 units and mining-contractor overburden removal to 766.0 million bank cubic metres as the national coal quota cut mining customers' capital spending [S14]. Coal sales fell to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales to 54,000 ounces after Martabe stopped producing early in the year [S14]. But the division's attributable profit rose year on year in the third quarter as contract volumes recovered and Martabe restarted [S14]. This is a policy-driven cycle in a business Astra controls through UNTR.

The competitive position is durable but not invulnerable. Toyota and Daihatsu retain the leading car brands and Honda is close to a monopoly in motorcycles, while the distribution-and-financing network raises switching costs and gives the financial arm a captive origination channel [S2, S4]. The threat is Chinese entrants and electrified models, which the group meets through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform [S9]. The heavy-equipment moat is Komatsu distribution plus the Pamapersada contractor, tied to the coal cycle [S2].

The state sets the coal quota and has already cut heavy-equipment demand [S14]; vehicle taxes and subsidies shape the car market [S9]. The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E and Bank Indonesia's policy rate at 5.75 per cent, with inflation at 3.3%; a consumer-durable and consumer-financing group is rate-sensitive [S2, S4].

FY2025 profit before tax was IDR49,288.0bn against EBIT of IDR38,665.0bn; the gap is mainly IDR9.62tn of permanent equity-accounted Honda and Toyota income, with the balance other non-operating income net of finance costs, so not all of the below-operating line is recurring joint-venture income; net income was IDR32,769.0bn and earnings per share Rp815 [S6].

Nine-month revenue of IDR243.87tn was flat and gross profit of IDR52.01tn slightly lower, a gross margin just under twenty-two per cent [S15]. That is below FY2025 because of the first-half Martabe outage and coal-quota hit; the third quarter ran at a materially better margin as mining and gold recovered [S14]. Costs rose faster than revenue: selling expenses were IDR10.41tn and administrative expenses IDR16.94tn, over eleven per cent of revenue against about ten per cent in FY2025, so operating profit fell even though revenue held [S15].

Reported net profit was IDR21.60tn, but IDR2.96tn of the fall came from non-recurring impairment and fair-value adjustments on equity investments, principally geothermal and nickel [S14]. Profit before tax was IDR30.01tn, below the operating line other income turned to an expense of IDR2.43tn from income a year earlier, and the share of joint-venture results rose to IDR8.13tn [S15]. Clean of the charge, net profit was IDR24.57tn, down about one per cent, and clean earnings per share was slightly higher on the smaller share count [S14].

The data pack carries no depreciation line for this direct-method filer, so we restate it from the audited notes: IDR17.87tn in FY2025 and IDR16.70tn in FY2024 [S6]. On that basis FY2025 EBITDA was IDR56,536.0bn, an EBITDA margin of 17.5% [S6].

Cash generation is the strongest quality signal. Operating cash flow was IDR28.61tn over nine months, above consolidated profit even as financing receivables grew [S15, S14]. Capital expenditure was IDR17,440.0bn in FY2025 and ran lower in the first nine months; dividends paid were IDR16,426.0bn, a payout of 50.0% the company describes as its policy ratio [S15, S0, S4].

The balance sheet reads better at the holding-company level. Group net debt was IDR56,315.0bn at FY2025 [S0], but almost all sits inside the financing subsidiaries, whose net debt was IDR66.70tn at September 2026 [S14]. Excluding them the group was back to net cash of IDR1.80tn [S14], lower after the February 2026 PT Arafura Surya Alam gold-mine acquisition bought through United Tractors and carried inside its market mark [S15, S14]; parent equity rose to IDR238.10tn [S15]. The dividend-upstream test passes on the parent-entity-only statements: the parent received IDR18.99tn of cash dividends from its subsidiaries in FY2025 while paying IDR16.43tn to its own shareholders [S6]; the consolidated investing line nets out subsidiary dividends and is not this flow [S6].

Our forecast anchors on the actual nine months. Revenue grows 1.0% to IDR326,625.9bn, the flat nine months needing only the guided fourth-quarter step-up [S14]. The FY2026E gross margin of 21.7% and operating costs of 11.1% of revenue come from the nine-month actual and a fourth quarter at the third quarter's rate, giving operating profit of IDR34,524.4bn and an EBITDA margin of 16.1% [S15, S14]. From FY2027E the gross margin returns to the FY2025 audited rate while operating costs stay at the third-quarter 10.8%, because no sourced cost programme justifies the lower ratio [S15, S6]. Other income is the clean nine-month run-rate annualised at IDR11,548bn, and the minority take starts at the clean nine-month share then restores toward the FY2025 audited IDR7,436.0bn of IDR40,205.0bn as mining recovers [S15, S0]. Net income attributable to the parent is IDR33,362.8bn clean, broadly flat, then IDR35,087.6bn in FY2027E and IDR41,892.9bn by FY2030E; the forecast excludes the non-recurring charge, and the FY2026E margin gap to FY2025 is the nine-month cost ratio carried forward, not a cost assumption [S15, S6].

Earnings-quality flags, run at both levels. **Accruals** are clean: operating cash flow exceeded net profit in each of FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 [S0], and again over nine months at IDR28.61tn [S15], so the three-year accruals ratio is negative in every year. **Non-recurring items** are optics-class: the IDR2.96tn charge is disclosed, non-cash and tied to equity investments, but we strip it before applying any multiple [S14]. **Margin and cost divergence** is the flag to follow: costs grew while revenue was flat, and we hold the higher ratio rather than banking operating leverage [S15]. **Financing-book provisioning** is the right test for the lender: the charge was built, not released, at IDR1.16tn in the first half while receivables grew to IDR132.00tn [S5, S14]. **Related-party gravity**: purchases were IDR84.94tn in FY2025 and sales IDR27.94tn [S6]; operating structures, not value leakage. **Auditor** and **IDX notation** are open checks: the archived LK omits the audit report and idx.co.id is not retrieved by policy, though no going-concern, late-filing or special-monitoring notice appears in any archived disclosure [S6]. **Fixed-asset revaluation** was immaterial at IDR0.00tn in FY2025 [S6]. **Structure flags**: no pledged controlling stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement was found [S6].

This is a holding company with listed and unlisted parts, so the industry method set applies: a sum-of-the-parts carrying 96% of the weight, cross-checked by own-history earnings and book multiples at 2% and 2% [S0].

The cost of equity is 14.9% and WACC 11.9%, built from a risk-free rate of 7.4% less the sovereign spread of 1.6%, a levered beta of 1.36 (unlevered 0.90, geared for debt-to-market-capitalisation of 0.66) and a mature-market risk premium of 4.2% plus country risk of 2.5% [S0].

The primary method is a look-through sum of the parts. The listed stakes — United Tractors at the effective post-buyback 62.1%, Astra Agro Lestari at 79.7% and Astra Graphia at 76.9% — go in at market [S6]; UNTR is the whole mining division. Automotive and financial services are marked on nine-month attributable income, IDR9.79tn and IDR7.15tn [S15], held at the nine-month average rather than extrapolating the stronger third quarter because management guides its drivers to continue into the fourth [S14]. The financing block's book/ROE-COE card must match the income basis: the income includes the segment's share of joint-venture results, so the book includes joint-venture investments of IDR9.28tn [S15] against segment liabilities of IDR97.84tn [S15]. On that wider book the annualised return is above the 14.9% cost of equity, so the block is carried at a justified premium to book [S15]. The wider unlisted blocks stay on the group's own-history multiple because the nine-month disclosure no longer splits them [S0], and property is marked on recurring earnings, stripping the IDR0.46tn bargain-purchase gain from the reported IDR0.72tn [S6, F29]. The bridge deducts parent-entity net debt — short-term borrowings of IDR5.05tn against cash of IDR2.64tn [S15]; the group's net cash excluding the financing subsidiaries of IDR1.80tn [S14] sits inside the marks and is not added again. The packet's bridge line prints the group's own consolidated net debt at the last half-year — borrowings less cash across the whole group — as a memo, group-level EV item used only by the EV-based cross-checks; it is not deducted a second time from the parts, because almost all of it is the financing subsidiaries' own funding against their receivables and the balance sits inside the market-valued stakes, so the display is not a double count of the parent net debt deducted above.

The cross-checks sit above the primary method: the P/E gives Rp5,911 and P/BV Rp6,647, respectively 31.0% and 47.3% above the sum-of-the-parts [S0]. They diverge because they are undiscounted while the parts carry a 25% discount, because P/BV uses the 30 September 2026 book value of IDR238.10tn [S15], and because the four-year averages were struck when the mining block earned several times what it earns now — H1-2025 mining attributable profit was IDR4.98tn against IDR0.61tn a year later [S5]. A multiple set on a mining-heavy mix is not a value we will bank for a group now weighted toward auto and financing, so the own-history multiples (7.2x earnings, 1.1x book, from the pack's four annual observations) carry 2% and 2% each as cross-checks, not as the cheapness case [S0, S5].

**Target construction.** The target is not the sum-of-the-parts itself: it is the blended mark of Rp4,585 compounded at the 14.9% cost of equity and net of the Rp420 of dividends paid over the twelve months, which gives Rp4,849 [S15, S0]. The roll is the largest single component of the gap and the dividend subtracts part of it. There is no separate discount-convergence term: the target uses the same 25% discount we hold throughout, so most of the expected return is the cost of capital rather than a re-rating.

Today's price is essentially our mark. Solving for the holdco discount that reproduces Rp4,540, the market prices a 24.6% discount to our marks [S14, S2] — fractionally narrower than the 25% we hold, so the target assumes no convergence. Against the name's own history that discount is wide: every one of the pack's four annual P/BV observations sits above today's 0.8x, against a four-year average of 1.1x [S0]. We do not put that narrowing in the base, because the only named catalyst is an undated buyback [S8]; the base assumes the group keeps earning its cost of equity, and the bear is where it does not [S14].

The scenario spread is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity on today's marks. The engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at their sourced actuals in every case, so the table does not reprice United Tractors, Astra Agro Lestari or the financing book: the bear's transmission is the wider discount plus group-level revenue, margin and joint-venture shocks. A bear reprice of the commodity stakes, or provisioning that cut the financing return below the cost of equity, would take the value below the tabulated bear [S14, S5].

**Regulatory and commodity risk — high likelihood, material impact.** The state sets the coal quota, already cutting heavy-equipment demand, and taxes and subsidies shape the car market; Astra controls neither lever [S14, S9]. Coal, gold, nickel and palm oil all run through earnings, and mining is the most volatile block [S4, S14].

**Macro and currency risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The house desk carries the rupiah at 18,350 per dollar for FY2027E and is cautious on Indonesian rate-sensitive demand; a consumer-durable and consumer-financing group is exposed on both the purchase decision and the credit book [S2, S4]. The desk's tilt avoids Indonesian rate-sensitive names; we do not override it. The caution sits in the 25% bear probability, the country risk premium in the 14.9% cost of equity, and a modest financing premium rather than a re-rating multiple; we do not cut the base margin on an unsourced view. The ADD is a valuation-and-return call, not a bet on a rate-sensitive re-rating.

**Competitive and technology risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** Chinese entrants and electrified models threaten the auto franchise, which the group meets through Toyota's range rather than a proprietary platform; automotive carries the top weight in the sum of the parts, so a share or mix loss is the largest value risk [S9, S14].

**Credit and provisioning risk — medium likelihood, material impact.** The financing block is IDR66.70tn of net debt against a receivables book of IDR132.00tn and grew new financing to IDR92.50tn. The IDR1.16tn first-half provisioning charge is the trend we watch: a full year at that rate would cut the block's return below the cost of equity and pull its premium to book toward one. The engine does not reprice the financing mark inside a scenario, so that credit risk reaches the table only through the wider discount and group income shocks; we state the limitation rather than imply the block is scenario-tested [S5, S14, F35].

**Governance and control risk — high likelihood, structural impact.** Jardine Cycle & Carriage holds 50.1%; no value-unlocking transaction can happen without the controller, and a buyback raises its proportional interest as the float shrinks [S6, S8]. The discount can widen while holders wait, which is why the base case holds it flat and the bull case carries the narrowing.

**Liquidity and dividend risk — low.** The shares turn over IDR232.7bn a day, and the parent received more in dividends than it paid in FY2025 while the interim was held at the prior year's level [S0, S6, S10]; a deeper mining downturn would pressure the payout.

The base case (50%) carries the actual nine months: revenue 1.0% this year and 5.0% thereafter, the higher cost ratio, the discount held at 25% with no narrowing, and the buyback retirement at the pace of the completed programme (-1.3% this year, -2.0% next) [S14]; it gives Rp4,849, which is the cost-of-equity roll. The bull case (25%) assumes share gains, a richer mix, the gold ramp and wider-business reallocation, the coal quota resetting and the buyback narrowing the discount below its range; it values the shares at Rp5,780. The bear case (25%) assumes coal and palm oil weaken, the quota stays tight, credit costs rise, joint-venture income falls, auto share is lost and the discount widens to the top of its range; it values the shares at Rp3,917, below the price. The shocks are mirrored, so an asymmetry needs a sourced reason and is not embedded [S14].

Signposts that would change our view: a wholesale run-rate consistent with the industry target while Astra's share holds [S7, S14]; Komatsu and mining-contractor volumes extending the third-quarter improvement [S14]; capital-allocation action on wider businesses [S11]; disclosed buyback execution [S8]; and any deterioration in upstream dividend coverage [S6].

Jardine Cycle & Carriage Ltd held 50.1% at the last audited date and is part of the Jardine Matheson group; the free float is 49.0% [S6, S0]. No pledged stake, serial rights issue or discounted affiliate placement is disclosed, and minorities have no route to a control event; the route to value is the dividend, the buyback and the controller's decisions [S6, S8, S11].
Related-party purchases were IDR84.94tn in FY2025 and sales IDR27.94tn, principally the Honda, Toyota and Daihatsu joint ventures [S6]: operating architecture, not value leakage [S6].

Capital actions are the main governance signal. The group completed IDR10.00tn of buybacks to September 2026, and the IDR8.00tn Astra programme approved in July is still running with no disclosed end date [S14, S16]. Astra is also offering for up to 4.95 per cent of Astra Otoparts at Rp3,600 a share, lifting its stake to 84.95 per cent [S13, S14]; that is a cash outlay inside an already consolidated block, and whether it adds value depends on the offer price against AUTO's market price, which is not in our pack, so we do not value it separately [S14, S13]. The board has independent commissioners and a separately constituted audit committee, but the auditor's identity and opinion wording remain open because the archived LK omits the audit report [S6].

Dividends per share were Rp650, Rp519, Rp406 and Rp390 across the last four financial years [S0], with a Rp98 interim declared for FY2026 at the prior year's level [S10]. On ESG, the material exposures are coal, palm oil and nickel, and the vehicle franchise's transition risk, which the group meets through its Japanese partners rather than a platform it owns [S14, S9].

The dated catalysts are the interim dividend paid at the end of October, the monthly wholesale data, the close of the Otoparts tender in November, and the FY2026 audited results in the spring, when buyback execution must be disclosed [S10, S7, S14, S4]. The interim was held at the prior year's level despite the profit fall, a signal on payout durability [S10].

Between updates we monitor five things: national car wholesales and Astra's share [S7, S14]; Komatsu units and overburden for evidence the quota downturn has troughed [S14]; net cash excluding the financing subsidiaries [S14]; buyback execution against the authorised amount [S14, S8]; and the parent's dividends received from subsidiaries against dividends paid, on the parent-entity statements [S6].

bear.narrative: The national RKAB coal quota stays tight and coal prices fall, so the mining complex does not recover: over nine months Komatsu units were already down 17% to 3,000, overburden down 7% to 766 million bcm, coal sales down 23% to 7.1 million tonnes and gold sales down to 54,000 oz after the Martabe stoppage [S14, F53, F54, F55, F56]; H1-2026 mining attributable profit of Rp607bn compares with Rp4,982bn in H1-2025 [S5, F30, F77]. Financial-services credit costs rise as a rate-sensitive CAUTIOUS macro lifts arrears: the financing book carried a Rp1,160bn H1 provisioning charge against Rp132.0tn of receivables and Rp66.7tn of net debt [S5, S14, F35, F51, F60]. The auto franchise loses share and mix to Chinese and electrified entrants [S9], JV income falls by Rp2,000bn, and the holdco discount widens to 40%, the top of the card's persistent 20-40% range, as the buyback fails to close it [S8, S14]. The holdco_sotp engine holds the listed stakes at market and the unlisted blocks at their sourced actuals in every case, so the tabulated bear is a discount-and-earnings sensitivity: a bear reprice of the United Tractors, Astra Agro Lestari or financing marks would take the value below the figure shown here, and the financing book's credit cost reaches the scenario only through the wider discount and the group-level income shocks.

bull.narrative: The auto market reaches GAIKINDO's 850,000-unit target with Astra holding about half of it [S7, S4], the national coal quota resets and the mining complex stabilises (this is a bull assumption, not in the base), the Martabe restart and the wider-business reallocation roadmap add earnings - nine-month Others attributable profit was already Rp2,558bn, up 36% [S11, S14, F71] - share gains and a richer mix lift the auto margin, and the ongoing Rp8tn buyback plus the capital-allocation framework narrow the holdco discount to 10%, below the card's persistent range [S8, S14, S11]. As in the bear, the engine does not reprice the listed stakes or the financing mark in this case, so a re-rating of United Tractors or Astra Agro Lestari and an acceleration of the buyback would add to the tabulated bull.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at +1%: nine-month 2026 net revenue was Rp243.9tn, flat on the prior-year period [S14, S15], with the third quarter alone up about six per cent on the prior-year quarter as automotive and financial services grew; reaching +1% for the full year needs only a small fourth-quarter step-up, which the company guides to on mining-contract volumes, the Martabe restart and continued auto growth [S14]. From FY2027E a 5% nominal growth, below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation [KB macro deck] but above the old 4% - the auto franchise is recovering and the group now reports three core businesses [S2].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 21.69%, the full-year rate implied by the nine-month actual (gross profit Rp52,008bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, 21.3%) plus a fourth quarter at the third quarter's 22.75% [S15]; the first half was depressed by the Martabe gold-mine outage and the RKAB coal quota, both of which eased in the third quarter [S14]. From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited 22.09% (gross profit Rp71,444bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S6]), which reproduces the third-quarter exit run-rate rather than the disrupted first half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 11.12% of full-year revenue, and the build is explicit: the nine months are the actual, selling and general expenses of Rp27,353bn on net revenue Rp243,869bn, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15], and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue rather than the bare 11.22% nine-month ratio. The prior 10.14% FY2025 ratio no longer describes the run-rate. From FY2027E held at the third-quarter 10.84% [S15]: the three-quarter cost ratio is the last actual and no sourced cost programme justifies reverting to the pre-2026 10.14% ratio, so the forecast carries the higher run-rate rather than banking an unsourced efficiency gain.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 D&A of Rp17,871bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn from the audited expenses-by-nature note [S6] (the data pack carries no depreciation line for IDX filers); held flat, with capex at the same years level so the fixed-asset base is stable. H1-2026 D&A was Rp8.7tn on Rp157.9tn of revenue, in line [S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 audited actual, capex Rp17,440bn on net revenue Rp323,392bn [S0]; the group reported H1-2026 capital expenditure of Rp5.2tn on a cash basis, Rp6.4tn including leased assets and concession rights [S5], against Rp8.2tn in H1-2025 [S3], so the FY2025 ratio is at the top of the recent range and is not raised.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held at zero: the segment note shows consolidated net debt of Rp73.0tn at 30 June 2026, of which Rp67.0tn sits in the financial services segment that funds itself against its own receivables book, and the non-financial segments are net of only Rp6.0tn [S5]; no new group funding is assumed.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E rebuilt from the clean nine-month actual, not a rounded-up run-rate: share of joint-venture results was Rp8,127bn for nine months, up from Rp6,769bn a year earlier [S15], and other (expenses)/income net was a Rp2,429bn expense that includes the Rp2,963bn non-recurring impairment and fair-value charge [S15, S14]; adding that charge back leaves about Rp534bn of clean other income, so clean nine-month other non-operating income is Rp8,127bn + Rp534bn = Rp8,661bn [S15, S14]. Annualising the nine months at 4/3 gives Rp11,548bn, which is the FY2026E anchor (no unsourced fourth-quarter step-up). From FY2027E held at the FY2025 audited Rp10,702bn (profit before tax Rp49,288bn less EBIT Rp38,665bn plus finance costs Rp3,734bn less interest income Rp3,655bn [S6]), the joint-venture anchor, so the elevated 2026 JV print is not capitalised into the long run. A JV-income shock is carried in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at 9.5%, the clean nine-month actual: reported profit for the period was Rp24,073bn including the Rp2,963bn non-recurring charge, so clean consolidated profit was about Rp27,036bn and clean profit attributable to non-controlling interests was about Rp2,471bn (Rp27,036bn less the Rp24,565bn clean parent profit), a 9.1% take [S12, S14, S15]. The mining business that carries United Tractors' 40.5% minority collapsed while the wholly owned automotive and financing blocks grew, so the three-year-average 21.4% take is not the 2026 path. From FY2027E the take rises to 14% and 15% long run: the base has mining recovering (gross margin back to the FY2025 audited rate and revenue growing), and the FY2025 actual take was 18.5% (non-controlling interests of Rp7,436bn on Rp40,205bn of consolidated profit [S0]), so a mining recovery must lift the minority share toward - not away from - the last audited level. The wholly owned auto and financing mix keeps the long-run take below that 18.5% actual; a UNTR-recovery sensitivity sits in the bear/bull shocks on revenue, margin and other income.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Held at the FY2025 actual of 50% (cash dividends paid Rp16,426bn by the parent entity over FY2025 parent net profit [S6]); the company itself reports a 48% payout ratio for FY2025 on the proposed Rp390 per share total dividend [S4], and declared the same Rp98 interim for FY2026 [S10], so the policy is being held, not raised.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: FY2026E set at -1.3%: nine-month EPS fell 11% to Rp541 while parent net profit fell 12%, implying a weighted-average share count about 1.3% lower year on year after the group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks between November 2025 and September 2026 [S14]. FY2027E set at -2.0%: the Rp8tn Astra programme approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM is authorised, on-going and undated [S8, S14, S16], so rather than assume zero retirement we carry it at the only sourced pace - the Group completed Rp10.0tn of buybacks over the eleven months to September 2026 [S14, F65]. At that rate about half of the authorised amount could retire within FY2027E, roughly 2% of the share count at the current price. We stop after one year rather than assume completion, because no end date or pace is disclosed; any residual and any acceleration stay in the bull case. FY2028E onward is held at zero and the completed to-September retirement is already in the FY2026E share count [S14].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set at 4%, below the house IDR terminal cap of 5% and below the macro deck's implied nominal growth (5.29% real GDP plus 3.28% inflation); it only feeds the reverse-DCF and the cross-checks, as the primary SOTP method carries no terminal value.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: Set at 25%, inside the 20-40% persistent range the holdco method card makes the base rate. The name-specific test is whether that is wide against the shares' own history: across the data pack's four annual price observations the shares traded between roughly 0.9x and 1.2x book [S0], while today's price is 0.76x the 30 September 2026 book value of Rp5,999 a share [S15], so the current mark is at the wide end of the name's own range rather than the low end. At this discount the SOTP sits essentially at the market price - the market-implied discount is within a point of the one we hold - so the base case does NOT assume any discount narrowing; the expected return is the cost-of-equity roll plus the dividend, and the rating is a return call rather than a narrowing call. The only named narrowing catalyst is the Rp8tn buyback approved at the 17 July 2026 EGM and still ongoing, alongside the May-2026 capital-allocation roadmap [S8, S14, S11]; it is authorised but undated, so narrowing is in the bull case only.

challenges.challenge: The bear and bull TPs are almost entirely the holdco-discount shock. Since the SOTP (96% weight) marks UNTR/AALI/ASGR at fixed market prices and auto/finserv/infra/property on fixed facts (F68/F69/F7/F9), the revenue -3%, gross-margin -1.2pp and JV -Rp2,000bn shocks only move the 2%+2% P/E and P/BV cross-checks. Bear TP Rp4,043 is essentially 'discount 25%->40% on today's marks', so the narrative (coal collapse, credit costs, auto share loss) does not reach the primary method.
challenges.answer: Relabelled the scenario table as a discount-and-earnings sensitivity and stated the engine limitation in the section lead: the listed stakes stay at market and the unlisted blocks at their sourced actuals in every case, so the bear's transmission is the wider discount plus group revenue, margin and joint-venture shocks and the bull's is the reverse. The base, bull and bear narratives now say that a commodity reprice or provisioning below the cost of equity would take the value below the tabulated bear rather than implying those risks are inside it. Scenario shocks can only target model inputs in this build, so disclosure is the available remedy; the credit limitation is repeated in the risk paragraph.

challenges.challenge: The report states the SOTP is Rp4,657 (above Rp4,540) and the target is Rp5,006, but never explains the 7.5% gap. The packet shows target = SOTP x (1 + COE 14.94%) - next-12m DPS 420, i.e. a full year of COE roll plus a 1.9pp discount-gap convergence. A reader cannot reconcile the two numbers or see that most of the target is the roll.
challenges.answer: Added a Target construction paragraph to section 4 that states the mechanics directly: the target is the blended mark compounded at the cost of equity and net of twelve months of dividends, target equals v0 times one plus COE minus dps12, and the roll is identified as the largest single component of the gap with the dividend subtracting part of it. The paragraph also states there is no separate discount-convergence term, because the target uses the same discount held throughout; the convergence component is therefore zero by construction and the reader can reconcile the parts value to the target.

challenges.challenge: The ADD is a COE-return call: with the SOTP only 2.6% above price, expected return 19.5% = 4.0% discount convergence + 14.9% COE roll + dividend. The §5 text says the base 'holds the discount at 25%', but holding 25% against a 26.9% implied discount is itself a 1.9pp narrowing. The only named narrowing catalyst, the Rp8tn buyback, was approved 17 July 2026, has no disclosed end date, and is carried only in the bull case; catalyst_date 2027-04-30 dates the disclosure, not the action.
challenges.answer: Reframed the rating as a cost-of-equity return call throughout: the investment summary, section 4 and section 5 now say the ADD is the cost-of-equity roll net of the dividend and not a discount-narrowing call. The base assumes the discount stays at the held level with no convergence, and the text states the market-implied discount is fractionally narrower than the held one, so nothing is assumed to narrow. The buyback is described as authorised, on-going and undated, carried only in the bull case, and the catalyst note says 30 April 2027 dates the disclosure, not the action, so it is not a dated narrowing catalyst in the base.

challenges.challenge: Thesis bullet 1 calls the stock cheap on 5.57x FY2025 P/E and 0.80x P/BV against 7.20x and 1.11x four-year averages - exactly the evidence carried by the P/E (Rp5,911) and P/BV (Rp6,647) cross-checks, which the valuation weights 2% each. The 96/2/2 weights neutralise the two methods that are +27% and +43% from the SOTP, so the report advertises cheapness it then discards.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now justifies the token weight rather than advertising cheapness it discards. The cross-checks are undiscounted while the parts carry the holdco discount, P/BV uses the current book value, and the four-year averages were struck on a mining-heavy mix, with the first-half mining profit collapse cited alongside. The text states the multiples are cross-checks, not the cheapness case, and thesis bullet 1 no longer cites own-history P/E and P/BV as the value case. We did not give them greater weight because a multiple set on a mix that no longer exists would raise the target on stale evidence.

challenges.challenge: Financial services is ~28% of the SOTP and the most rate/credit-sensitive block, yet the bear expresses credit risk only through group margin, JV and other income. No shock hits the finserv ROE/P/B mark (e.g. provisioning/ROE down), despite 'Credit and provisioning risk - medium likelihood, material impact' and a CAUTIOUS / AVOID-rate-sensitive macro deck.
challenges.answer: The financing mark was corrected to the equity base that matches its income, which lowers the premium to book and is the main reason the target fell. Credit risk is now explicit in the risk section: a full year at the first-half provisioning charge would take the block's return below the cost of equity and pull its premium toward one, and the text states the engine cannot reprice the holding inside a scenario so that risk reaches the table only through the wider discount and group income shocks. The macro reconciliation is also explicit: the desk's avoid tilt on rate-sensitive names is honoured through the bear probability, the country risk premium and a modest financing premium rather than a re-rating multiple, and the ADD is framed as a valuation-and-return call.

challenges.challenge: UNTR (Rp54.2tn, the largest SOTP row) and AALI (Rp14.6tn) are marked at today's market prices. In the bear, coal and palm oil weaken by the narrative but neither market mark is repriced, so the mining/agri legs have no downside in the scenario that is supposed to carry it. The bear understates the largest source of value risk.
challenges.answer: Took the disclosure remedy: the section 5 lead states the listed stakes are held at market and the unlisted blocks at sourced actuals in every scenario, so the bear does not reprice United Tractors, Astra Agro Lestari or the financing book, and the narrative says a commodity reprice would take the value below the tabulated bear. The bull mirrors the same omission, so the asymmetry is not one-sided. No sourced bear price or multiple exists in the pack for either stake, so a haircut would be an unsourced invention rather than evidence.

challenges.challenge: Automotive is marked on 9M attributable income x 4/3 = Rp13,049bn at 7.2x, +15% on FY2025's Rp11,365bn and above the LTM figure of ~Rp12,119bn (Q4-2025 auto = Rp2,332bn). This capitalises a Q3 peak (national market +21%, share recovering) into the 38%-of-SOTP auto mark without a source that the Q4 run-rate persists; the 4/3-vs-LTM choice is worth ~Rp170/share.
challenges.answer: Kept the nine-month annualisation but made it sourced and transparent. The release guides its drivers to support fourth-quarter performance and carries the weaker first nine months as the actual, so the forecast takes the fourth quarter at the third quarter's rate rather than assuming a repeat of the peak. The holding note now discloses that the group's four-year average multiple is grossed up by four thirds against the nine-month fact, giving the effective multiple shown, and states why FY2025 audited income would understate a block already at most of the prior year. The method and its LTM alternative are visible to the reader; the prose in section 3 and section 4 now says the mark uses nine-month figures and why.

challenges.challenge: The finserv ROE-COE card uses book equity of Rp47,169bn (segment assets 145,007 less liabilities 97,838), but S15 shows the segment's fin-serv column also holds 'Investasi pada ventura bersama dan entitas asosiasi' of Rp9,284bn and a second total-assets line of Rp154,291bn. Total segment equity is therefore Rp56,453bn; on it the annualised income gives ROE 16.9%, not 20.2%, and justified P/B 1.18 not 1.48 - the Rp69.9tn mark is overstated by ~Rp3.4tn (~Rp86/share). If instead the segment income excludes JV results, the Rp9,284bn of JV investments is an omitted asset. Either way the card is internally inconsistent.
challenges.answer: Corrected. The segment income includes its share of joint-venture and associate results, so the equity base now includes the segment's joint-venture investments against segment liabilities. On that wider book the annualised return is 16.9%, not the 20.2% computed on the excluding-JV equity, justified P/B is 1.178x, and the mark falls accordingly; the effective multiple on the nine-month fact is disclosed. Facts for the segment JV investments and the second total-assets line were added with verbatim quotes and page locators.

challenges.challenge: The report says 'the parent received IDR18.99tn in FY2025 while paying IDR16.43tn to its own shareholders', calling it the dividend-upstream test. F12 (S6) is the consolidated cash-flow 'Dividend kas yang diterima' line under investing activities - dividends received on investments/associates, not dividends upstreamed from consolidated subsidiaries (those are eliminated). F22 (16,426) is parent dividends paid. The comparison is real cash-in but not the sub-to-parent coverage the method card calls the most honest quality metric.
challenges.answer: The premise is incorrect. F12 and F22 are both taken from the parent-entity-only statements of cash flows on page 141 of the audited FY2025 accounts, not from the consolidated statement; both fact locators state that and the quotes are the parent lines (cash dividends received of 18,986 against 19,919; cash dividends paid of 16,426 against 20,998). The consolidated investing line, 10,015 against 9,850, is a different line and is not the one cited. The report now states the parent-entity basis explicitly and says the consolidated line nets out subsidiary dividends and is not this flow, so the coverage test stands as written. No fact change was needed.

challenges.challenge: share_change is 0.0% for FY2027E-2035E on the argument that the Rp8tn buyback has no end date. But it is authorised and on-going; at 0.76x book, retiring up to Rp8tn (~4% of the share count) is per-share accretive, and the Otoparts tender lifts the parent's economic stake from 80% to 84.95%. All are relegated to the bull case or ignored, an unowned conservatism.
challenges.answer: The base now retires stock at the completed programme's pace rather than assuming zero: the share change for the next financial year is set to a two per cent reduction, derived from the buybacks completed between November 2025 and September 2026 against market capitalisation, with the basis cited in the assumption. Otoparts is treated as a cash outlay inside an already consolidated block whose value effect depends on the offer price against AUTO's market price, which is not in the pack, so it is not valued separately and its direction is not asserted.

challenges.challenge: The wider businesses are marked on stale FY2025 figures - infrastructure at 7.2x Rp1,258bn and property at 2.554x the recurring Rp255bn - while the 9M 'Others' attributable profit is Rp2,558bn, +36%, driven partly by the newly acquired industrial-warehouse platform (S14). The May-2026 earn-or-reallocate roadmap and any asset-sale/sub-IPO proceeds are not valued. The base ignores a real, sourced improvement.
challenges.answer: Explained rather than inflated: the nine-month disclosure reports the wider businesses only inside the aggregated Others line, so infrastructure and property keep the last audited divisional figures, with property already marked on recurring earnings after stripping the bargain-purchase gain. The infrastructure note records the Others profit improvement and says it is carried in the bull case rather than marked in the base, and the roadmap's earn-or-reallocate test and any capital action are named as upside signposts rather than valued. A nine-month run-rate cannot be split by block from the available source, so marking it would be an allocation we cannot support.

challenges.challenge: minority_pct is set to 11.5% FY2027E and 12% long-run, 'partial restoration' toward a stated 3-year average of 21.4%. The FY2025 actual was ~18.5% (NCI Rp7,436bn on Rp40,205bn profit). As UNTR (40.5% minority) recovers in the base/bull, the minority take should rise toward - not stay far below - the actual, inflating NP parent.
challenges.answer: The minority take now restores faster and closer to the audited actual: 14 per cent next financial year, 15 per cent from the following year including the long-run rate, against the FY2025 actual of 18.5 per cent of profit. The section 3 text ties the restoration to mining recovery, which is in the base, so its minority drag is in the base. It stays slightly below the actual because the base holds mining below its historical share of group profit, and that gap is disclosed rather than left as an unexplained 12 per cent.

challenges.challenge: holdco_net_debt of -Rp1,800bn adds consolidated net cash excluding the finance subsidiaries (F50). That cash sits largely inside the market-valued UNTR/AALI stakes and the P/E-marked auto block, so adding it on top double counts ~Rp45/share; the parent holdco itself carries little net debt. The method card asks for holdco net debt, not group net cash.
challenges.answer: The bridge now deducts parent-entity net debt instead of adding group net cash: parent short-term borrowings less parent cash, both quoted from the parent-entity balance sheet, gives net debt of 2,410, and the previous negative bridge is reversed. Section 4 shows the reconciliation and says the group's net cash excluding the financing subsidiaries sits inside the market-valued stakes and the earnings-marked blocks and is not added again. The two parent balance-sheet facts were added with verbatim quotes and page locators.

challenges.challenge: Two citations overreach their sources: (i) 'Astra's share still reached 51.0% [S4]' rests on S4's 'pangsa pasar Astra dapat mencapai 51%' ('can reach'), a qualified statement, not a stated actual; (ii) the Otoparts tender is said to 'move value from minorities to the parent', but that depends on comparing Rp3,600 to AUTO's market price - if Rp3,600 is a premium, the transfer runs the other way. Neither is load-bearing to the number, but both say more than the source.
challenges.answer: Both overreaches removed. The market-share fact is relabelled as the company's stated achievable share (its wording is that the share can reach that level, not that it did), and section 2 now reads that the company said its share could reach that level when national sales were falling; no GAIKINDO FY2025 actual is in the pack to substitute. The Otoparts paragraph no longer asserts a transfer from minorities to the parent: it is described as a cash outlay inside an already consolidated block, with value dependent on the offer price against AUTO's market price, which is not in the pack, so no direction is claimed.

challenges.challenge: Section 3 states that the FY2025 profit-before-tax-to-EBIT gap is F10's 9,618 of equity-accounted Honda and Toyota income, but the report's own printed figures put PBT at 49,288 and EBIT at 38,665, a gap of 10,623 (other non-operating income of 10,702 net of finance costs of 79). Joint-venture income of 9,618 is the largest part of that gap, not the whole of it: the sentence contradicts the two figures it sits between and overstates how much of the below-EBIT result is permanent equity-accounted income rather than other income and financing. QC round 1 raised this as FIX Q3 and the draft still carries it.
challenges.answer: Accepted and fixed at the text level. Section 3 now says the profit-before-tax-to-EBIT gap is mainly the 9,618 of equity-accounted Honda and Toyota income, with the balance other non-operating income net of finance costs, so the sentence reconciles the 49,288 PBT and 38,665 EBIT it cites and no longer equates the whole gap with the joint-venture line. The gap is 10,623 (other non-operating 10,702 less net finance 79) and the prose now says "mainly" rather than implying the JV income is all of it. No model input, fact or valuation figure changed; F10 is unchanged at 9,618 and the placeholder is used as before.

missing_bull_case.note: Understated: (i) the on-going Rp8tn buyback plus UNTR/AALI buybacks and the Otoparts tender (80->84.95%) are treated as 0% share change FY2027E; (ii) wider businesses (Others 9M +36%, new industrial-warehouse platform) are marked on stale FY2025 figures; (iii) the Honda-motorcycle JV (77% share, net cash) gets no quality premium inside the 7.2x auto mark.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear likely understates downside: finserv (28% of SOTP) has no rate/provisioning shock; UNTR/AALI stay at today's market price so a coal/palm fall does not move the largest SOTP block; auto share loss is only a -3% group-revenue / -1.2pp gross-margin shock.

assumption_realism.note: Auto marked on 9M x 4/3 (Rp13,049bn, +15% on FY2025) capitalises a Q3 peak at 7.2x (LTM would be ~Rp12,119bn); minority 12% long-run sits below the FY2025 actual ~18.5%. Both bias NP parent upward; neither is sourced beyond judgement.

evidence_and_citations.note: Dividend-upstream test uses the consolidated investing-cash-flow 'dividends received' line (S6, i.e. JV/associate dividends) as if it were sub-to-parent upstream; 51.0% FY2025 share is cited from 'dapat mencapai 51%' ('can reach'); the Otoparts transfer direction is asserted without AUTO's price vs Rp3,600.

valuation_method_fit.note: Scenario shocks move only the holdco discount for the 96%-weighted SOTP; revenue/GM/JV shocks touch only the 4% cross-checks. Finserv P/B uses equity Rp47,169bn = segment assets less liabilities, excluding Rp9,284bn of segment JV/associate investments (total segment equity Rp56,453bn), so ROE 20.2% vs 16.9% is overstated. The Rp5,006 target vs Rp4,657 SOTP is the undisclosed COE roll.

bias_and_tone.note: ADD depends on applying COE 14.9% to the SOTP (SOTP only 2.6% above price). The base embeds a 1.9pp discount narrowing (25% held vs 26.9% implied) while the named buyback catalyst is undated and carried only in the bull. Thesis bullet 1 cites own-history P/E and P/BV cheapness that the valuation weights 2% each.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Macro deck is CAUTIOUS and explicitly AVOID INDO rate-sensitive; the report is ADD on a rate-sensitive group without reconciling the tilt. BI rate quoted 5.8% vs deck 5.75%. Rupiah, GDP and CPI inputs match the deck.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservatism in share_change 0% FY2027E (buyback) and payout 50% (upstream coverage >1x) is offset by optimism in auto peak annualisation, the finserv equity base and 12% minority vs 18.5% actual. No single unsourced haircut is rating-dispositive, but the offset is not disclosed.

calibration.note: FY2026E EBITDA margin 16.10% vs FY2025A 17.48% (gap -1.39pp): actual-driven via the 9M cost ratio [S15] and FY2027E recovers, but the gate carries no qc_justification entry. Add one citing S15.

signoff.notes: APPROVED round 2. Re-read the packet and fund record qc block and re-ran draft lint (PASS, one word-count warning). The round-1 blocker Q3/L1 is resolved on substance: section 3 now states the FY2025 PBT-EBIT gap as mainly the 9,618 of equity-accounted JV income with the balance other non-operating income net of finance costs, and the prose no longer implies the JV line is the whole gap; the residual 10,623 reconciles to the printed PBT 49,288 less EBIT 38,665 (other non-operating 10,702 less net finance 79), which QC recomputed from the model and I confirmed against S6 and F10. The three remaining NOTEs are disclosure-only and now carried in the text: the 71,550 packet bridge line is labelled a memo group-level EV item while the SOTP deducts parent net debt 2,410 (Q1/Q6); the FY2026E opex basis spells out the Q4-at-Q3-rate step (Q2); the post-balance-sheet note carries the 11 February 2026 Arafura acquisition at USD540m inside UNTR's market mark (Q4). Q5 (3,617 words) and Q7 (scenario marks) were already noted in round 1 and are non-blocking. Model, target 4,849, SOTP 4,514 and expected return 16.1% are unchanged from round 1, so the round-1 bias conclusion stands: bias neutral, judge PASS, no shared-input tilt in the CONGLOMERATES batch (comps re-run, published calls still mixed and the holdco-discount schedule still monotonic in size and liquidity). The ADD remains a disclosed cost-of-equity return call with the SOTP at price, not a discount-convergence call. Approved; left at signoff for the Director to publish.

bias.note: Round 2. The model is unchanged since round 1 (target 4,849, SOTP 4,514, expected return 16.1%, COE 14.9%), so the round-1 bias conclusion stands and the revision was text-level only. Optimistic departures remain disclosed and sourced: the auto block is marked on 9M attributable income x4/3 (Rp13,049bn against an LTM of about Rp12,119bn, roughly 3.5% of target) [S14, F68], and the long-run minority take is 15% against the FY2025 actual 18.5% [S0, S15]. Countervailing conservatism: the 25% holdco discount is held with no narrowing although the name's own P/B range is 0.93-1.20x against 0.76x today [S0, S15], other non-operating income is reset to the FY2025 Rp10,702bn, the wider blocks stay on stale FY2025 marks, and the two construction corrections (finserv JV-inclusive book, parent net debt) cut about Rp157 per share. The engine drift flag (FY2026E EBITDA margin 16.10% against FY2025A 17.48%, -1.39pp) is the nine-month cost ratio carried forward, stated in §3 and sourced to the actual 11.22% nine-month opex ratio [S15, F41, F43, F44]; it is a forecast choice, not a mis-specified history, because FY2025A EBITDA reproduces at 56,536. Both directions net near zero; the judge independently returned neutral.

recomputed.item: FY2025 PBT-EBIT gap (PBT 49,288 - EBIT 38,665 = 10,623; other_nonop 10,702 less net finance 79)
Parent net debt in SOTP bridge (short-term borrowings 5,051 - cash 2,641)
Financial-services 9M2026 equity base (assets incl JV 154,291 - liabilities 97,838)
Arafura consideration USD540m = Rp9.1tn, 11 Feb 2026 via Danusa Tambang Nusantara

findings.finding: The packet's bridge line shows consolidated net debt of 71,550 (1H2026 debt 119,198 less cash 47,648) while the SOTP correctly deducts parent-entity net debt of 2,410; the SOTP is not double-counting, but the display invites that read.
findings.answer: Labelled as a memo item. Section 4 now states that the packet bridge line prints the group's own consolidated net debt at the last half-year - borrowings less cash across the whole group - as a memo, group-level EV item used only by the EV-based cross-checks, and that it is not deducted a second time from the parts because almost all of it is the financing subsidiaries' own funding against their receivables and the balance sits inside the market-valued stakes. The sum-of-the-parts deduction remains parent-entity net debt of 2,410 (F81 less F80) [S15], so the display cannot be read as double-counting. The packet line itself is generated from the data pack and fund record, which the analyst may not edit, so the label is carried in the report and in the post-balance-sheet note rather than in the display field.

findings.finding: FY2026E opex_pct of 11.12% against the bare 27,353/243,869 = 11.22% (F43+F44/F41); 11.12% is reproduced only with Q4 at the Q3 10.84% rate, which the basis text does not spell out.
findings.answer: The opex_pct basis now spells out the build: the nine months are the actual (selling and general expenses of 27,353 on net revenue of 243,869, or 11.22% of nine-month revenue [S15]) and the fourth quarter is taken at the third quarter's 10.84% rate as promotional spend normalised, so the year blends to 11.12% of full-year revenue rather than the bare 11.22% nine-month ratio. The input value is unchanged at 11.12%; only the explanation was missing.

findings.finding: Section 3 says 'the gap being' F10 (Rp9.62tn) between FY2025 PBT 49,288 and EBIT 38,665, but the gap is 10,623 (other_nonop 10,702 less net finance 79); joint-venture income of 9,618 is the largest part, not the whole.
findings.answer: Fixed, same edit as the Sector Lead's L1: section 3 now says the profit-before-tax-to-EBIT gap is mainly the 9,618 of equity-accounted Honda and Toyota income, with the balance other non-operating income net of finance costs, which reconciles to the 49,288 PBT and 38,665 EBIT printed in the same sentence. The gap is 10,623 (other non-operating 10,702 less net finance 79); the prose no longer states or implies that the JV line is the whole gap. No model input changed.

findings.finding: The post-balance-sheet note omits the 11 February 2026 acquisition of PT Arafura Surya Alam (100%, USD540m/Rp9.1tn, via UNTR's Danusa Tambang Nusantara), the main reason net cash ex-finserv fell to Rp1.8tn [S14, S15]; it sits inside the UNTR market mark so there is no value gap, but the searched-since note should name it.
findings.answer: Added as item (6) of the post-balance-sheet note: on 11 February 2026 the Group, through PT Danusa Tambang Nusantara, an indirect subsidiary of PT United Tractors Tbk, bought 100% of PT Arafura Surya Alam, a North Sulawesi gold miner, for USD540m, equivalent to Rp9.1tn [S15], which the release names alongside the buyback as the main reason cash fell [S14]. The note states it sits inside the UNTR market mark - United Tractors is valued at its market price, which already reflects the acquisition - so there is no separate value gap and nothing is bridged. Section 3's balance-sheet sentence also names it against the lower net cash excluding the financing subsidiaries.
